subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & batching assumptions (continuous batching)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lucas Barnes <lucas@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & batching assumptions (continuous batching)

Hi Lucas — great convo earlier today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can get you a scoped estimate: 

1) Traffic & token volumes (your input)
- Current: ~15–25M tokens / month across product search and summarization flows
- Expected ramp: 60–80M tokens / month within 6 months, potential to 150M+ by EOY if feature adoption hits target

2) Budget / unit economics (your guidance)
- Target blended cost range: ~$400–$600 per 1M tokens (goal is to keep inference cost predictable around this band)
- Initial monthly budget target: ~$7k–$12k to start, with room to expand as we validate latency and quality

3) Workload pattern & batching assumptions
- Continuous-batching profile: steady stream of small requests rather than large periodic bursts
- Average prompt length: ~150 tokens in, ~50 tokens out (avg total ~200 tokens per call)
- Sustained QPS: ~40–60 qps, daytime peak to ~180–220 qps for short windows
- Concurrency expectation: low per-request concurrency, rely on batching to improve throughput and unit cost
- Latency target: p95 < 300–400ms for the majority of interactive flows

Ask: can you confirm the current 15–25M/month figure and the expected ramp to 60–80M/month timeline? Also confirm whether 200-token average is a good proxy for our calcs. If you can send a quick usage export (CSV) that shows requests by timestamp and token counts, that will let us build a more precise cost estimate.

Next steps I propose:
- You: share a small usage export (CSV) with timestamps, request token counts (sample of last 30 days)
- Us: produce a quick hosted vs dedicated cost estimate (unit $/1M tokens + projected monthly) and a recommended configuration (continuous batching params, concurrency target, recommended model family)

Attaching an example CSV template and a short checklist for what we need.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: acme_usage_export_template.csv

From: Lucas Barnes <lucas@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 15:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & batching assumptions (continuous batching)

Thanks Camila — yep, good recap. Confirming the numbers from our side: 
- Current production usage is roughly 18M tokens/mo (avg of last 3 months).
- We plan to roll the new summarization feature to 50% of users in the next quarter which we estimate pushes us to ~65M tokens/mo in ~3–6 months.
- Long term (6–12 months) if adoption goes well we could hit 120–160M tokens/mo.

Budget: our Finance and Product leads are expecting a starting spend between $8k–$12k/mo and we want to see cost per 1M tokens in the $400–$600 band to feel comfortable scaling.

Workload patterns:
- The majority of calls are short (150 tokens in / 40–60 tokens out).
- Traffic profile is steady throughout the day with predictable peaks (no big nightly batch jobs). Continuous batching works well for us as long as p95 is <~400ms for user-facing flows.

I've attached a 30-day CSV export with timestamps and token counts (sanitized). Let me know if you need anything else.

—Lucas
Lucas Barnes
CTO | Acme Analytics
lucas@acmeanalytics.com | +1 (650) 555-0100

Attachments: acme_usage_export_mar2026.csv

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lucas Barnes <lucas@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 16:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & batching assumptions (continuous batching)

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the CSV, Lucas — that helps a lot. High-level takeaways from a quick pass:
- Verified baseline: ~18M/mo current; projected ~65M/mo in 3–6 months matches what you described
- Avg tokens/call in CSV: ~195 tokens (aligned with 150 in / 45 out) — good to use 200 tokens per call for estimates
- Traffic pattern: steady with short peaks — continuous batching will be effective here and should materially reduce per-token cost vs naive per-request execution

Proposed next steps from Redwood: 
1) Preliminary hosted estimate (ballpark): $520 per 1M tokens (blended for your mix of short-generation + summarization). This is a preliminary list price for hosted inference; final negotiated rate may vary based on commitment level and contract term.
2) Dedicated capacity (if you want predictable latency and isolation) — we can generate a dedicated capacity estimate next; given current volumes, a dedicated pool becomes attractive at sustained 60M+ tokens/mo but depends on your desired SLOs.
3) Technical prescriptive: we recommend enabling continuous batching with max batch windows of 50–80ms and batching-based concurrency tuning (target effective batching concurrency of 8–16 per worker). That configuration tends to hit a good cost/latency sweet spot for Redis/KV-cache friendly gen models for 200-token avg calls.

Could I ask Aditya to look over the quick price band above and approve moving to a formal estimate (hosted vs dedicated)? If approved, we'll prepare a two-option quote (hosted list + dedicated baseline) and an ops runbook with recommended batching parameters.

If that sounds good I can turn the hosted estimate into a slide and spreadsheet and send over a redlined MSA draft for your legal team to review.

Thanks —
Camila

On a related note — Lucas, do you have any hard p95 latency requirement under 200ms for any critical flows? If so please call that out and we can evaluate a dedicated configuration to hit stricter SLOs.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
